original: - Butyrate & SCFAs: While the small intestine runs on glutamine, the large intestine relies on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like butyrate. Getting these via raw resistant starch fermentation or your home-brewed SIBO yogurt fuels colonocytes, locks down the lower gut barrier, and systematically suppresses inflammatory signals.
rewrite: - Your small intestine runs on glutamine, but the colonocytes lining your large intestine rely on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like butyrate. You get them when your gut bacteria ferment raw resistant starch, or from your home-brewed SIBO yogurt. They feed the colonocytes, and well-fed colonocytes keep the barrier in your lower gut locked down. SCFAs also keep inflammatory signals turned down.
